subject: Next steps: security intake, pen-test handback & SLA
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hart <alex.hart@luminahealth.com>, Keeley Barnes <kbarnes@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Next steps: security intake, pen-test handback & SLA

Hi Alex / Keeley — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your security team what they need for procurement.

TL;DR
- Lumina asked for SOC 2 evidence, vendor questionnaire, and a recent pen-test report (or plan + expected handback).
- Internal: Rishi, can you propose a short SLA/scanning cadence and what we can share from a recent pen test?
- Action: Alex / Keeley to confirm SOC 2 status, preferred scope for the pen report (redacted vs. full), and any specific questionnaire format (Excel/Doc).

Details / asks
1) SOC 2: please confirm whether Lumina needs Type I or Type II evidence, and whether proof-of-compliance (attestation PDF) is sufficient for now. If you have a specific control matrix mapping we should align to, please send.

2) Pen test report: Lumina procurement typically wants either (A) the most recent pen test report with a standard redaction (no PII of testers), or (B) an attestation + executive summary if the full report is sensitive. We have a standard handback flow but want to understand Lumina's preference.

3) Vulnerability management / SLA: we typically operate on a 30/90/365 severity-driven SLA (critical/major/minor). Rishi will propose exact TTR/TTRSLAs and scan cadence (auth/unauth + agent/scheduled).

4) Questionnaire / intake: If you have a vendor security questionnaire, drop it here or in the HubSpot record and we can start the intake. We can also upload our standard security packet to a shared Drive.

Attachments: I attached a short POV list for the procurement team (Lumina_POC_Security_Notes.pdf) and a quick scope template (Lumina_ThirdParty_Scope.xlsx).

Proposed immediate timeline
- Today: Lumina confirms SOC 2 type and report preference.
- 48–72h: Redwood to share initial attestation + proposed SLA + disclosure policy draft.
- Within 7 business days: start questionnaire work or schedule a focused security Q&A with Rishi & Grace.

If this looks good I’ll tee up a DocuSign NDA (if needed) and a short intake call with Rishi.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0134
Email: tessa.morgan@redwood.com

From: Alex Hart <alex.hart@luminahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Keeley Barnes <kbarnes@luminahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 12:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: security intake, pen-test handback & SLA

Tessa — great walkthrough, thanks. Quick answers from our side:

- SOC 2: We require Type II for vendor onboarding but will accept an in-progress Type II with an expected completion date for initial pilots. Our compliance lead asked for estimated completion date and whether Redwood can share the attestation PDF once available.

- Pen test: For procurement we prefer an executive summary + remediation status for initial review. If we need the full report later, we can execute an NDA and then request the full PDF with standard redactions. Executive summary should include date, scope, high-level severity counts, and if any findings are open/triaged.

- Questionnaire: I’ve attached Lumina_Vendor_Q_2027.xlsx (we typically use Excel). If you can ingest it and return answers in the same workbook, that’s ideal.

We’ll also need to understand your vulnerability disclosure policy and escalation SLA (how quickly critical vulnerabilities are acknowledged / remediated).

I attached our procurement packet for reference (not the full PII).

—Alex
Alex Hart
Head of Procurement, Lumina Health
alex.hart@luminahealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Alex Hart <alex.hart@luminahealth.com>, Keeley Barnes <kbarnes@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: security intake, pen-test handback & SLA

Thanks — looping in some specifics from security/ops so procurement has an actionable SLA and disclosure position.

Summary (proposed)
- Pen-test handback: we can provide an executive summary and remediation status within 3 business days of request. For full reports we require a standard NDA + redaction of tester PII; we can deliver the full report within 7 business days of a signed NDA.

- Vulnerability SLA (proposed): Critical = acknowledge within 4 hours, mitigation plan within 48 hours; High = acknowledge within 24 hours, patch/mitigation timeline within 7 calendar days; Medium/Low = acknowledged within 3 business days, remediation per release cadence (30–90 days). We can commit to an agreed-upon TTR for pilots under contract.

- Scanning cadence: authenticated quarterly + unauthenticated weekly external scans (third-party ASV annually if required). For customers asking for more frequent checks we can add monthly authenticated scans for the in-scope assets under a dedicated engagement.

- Disclosure approach: public disclosure only with mutual coordination. Our standard: if a customer requires earlier disclosure we will follow the customer's disclosure policy after triage and mutually agreed redaction.

Attachments: I’m attaching our vulnerability disclosure & handback primer (Redwood_Vuln_Disclosure_v1.pdf) and a short checklist we use for pen-report handback (PenReport_Handback_Checklist.txt).

Questions for Lumina
1) Can you confirm which assets/services you consider in-scope for the initial review? (API endpoints, embedding store, console access, SSO integration).
2) Will Lumina accept the proposed SLA cadence or do you need Accelerated timelines for critical severity?

If you prefer, we can convert the proposed SLA into a short mutually-signed appendix for the pilot (saves time during procurement).

—Rishi Malhotra
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alex — this is helpful. Next steps from my side:
- I’ll upload the Lumina vendor questionnaire into our HubSpot record (HS-93420) and populate answers where we can.
- Rishi — please confirm whether the 3 business day exec summary + 7 business day full report window is okay to put into a pilot appendix. If Lumina confirms assets in-scope this week we can draft the appendix and send an initial DocuSign NDA for full report access.
- Keeley — if you can confirm the in-scope assets (API keys, SSO metadata, console admin URLs), we’ll scope the authenticated scan.

I’ve created a temporary shared folder and uploaded the two items I had (Lumina_POC_Security_Notes.pdf, Lumina_ThirdParty_Scope.xlsx). Link is in the HubSpot record. I’ll also start the NDA DocuSign and tag you both.

If everyone agrees, I’ll mark this thread as the canonical intake and follow up with an invite for a 30-minute security Q&A on Thursday (Rishi + Grace + Alex + Keeley).

Best,
Tessa
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
